candidate_threads.canonical_name: Administrative State Capture via DOGE and Civil-Service Purge
candidate_threads.description: Executive centralization of the federal bureaucracy through DOGE, civil-service purges, agency hollowing, politicized personnel control, and capture of payment and operating systems.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, oversight, and agencies are politicized and partially outsourced to Musk’s DOGE
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces DOGE, Schedule F, and loyalty-driven restructuring as an early governing method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, oversight, and labor protections are gutted to build a loyalty-based state
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the project expanding into HR data, watchdog removals, and destruction of labor and oversight protections.

supporting_developments.development_title: Musk’s DOGE apparatus and Trump loyalists capture the administrative state and federal payment infrastructure
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes explicit the move from staffing and structure into payment systems and agency operations.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOGE becomes a parallel executive state and spearheads a civil service purge
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows consolidation of the pattern into a parallel governing apparatus with operational reach.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOGE-Driven Purge Reshapes the Federal Workforce and Public Services
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same logic through mass layoffs and restructuring across public-facing agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Musk’s DOGE tightens control over federal money, data, and the civil service
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms that DOGE is not episodic but an ongoing method of controlling money, data, and staffing.

inclusion_notes: Include DOGE authority expansion, mass layoffs, buyouts, Schedule F, personnel-system control, and agency hollowing.
Include capture of payment systems, HR systems, and operational levers across agencies.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general corruption unless directly tied to capture of state machinery.
Exclude broad fiscal policy unless specifically about DOGE or bureaucratic control.
boundary_notes: Related to crony capitalism and private-state fusion, but focused on control of the federal apparatus itself.
Related to executive overreach, but narrower and more operational.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration, Citizenship, and Asylum as Tools of Tiered Belonging and Domestic Control
candidate_threads.description: Use of emergency powers, deportation machinery, detention, birthright attacks, and status precarity to create a stratified legal order and extend coercive state power.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, citizenship, and the border are recast as a permanent emergency
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes the emergency framework and militarized approach to immigration and citizenship.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, citizenship, and protest rights are recast through mass raids and tiered status
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into raids, Guantánamo, TPS changes, and protest-linked status vulnerability.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, asylum, and citizenship are restructured through hardline executive orders and offshored detention
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows asylum suspension, offshore detention, and citizenship attacks as recurring methods.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and public health are redefined along ideological and identity lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the thread through selective asylum, ICE operations, and identity-based access to protections.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and Citizenship Policy Harden Into a Tiered System of Rights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes the status hierarchy itself the center of the weekly development.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump accelerates mass deportation and a tiered immigration regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms continuity through mass-deportation ambition, surveillance, and monetized citizenship.

inclusion_notes: Include raids, detention expansion, Guantánamo use, asylum suspension, birthright citizenship attacks, TPS and status changes, and legal precarity.
Include uses of immigration law against dissent, local autonomy, or public participation when clearly linked.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic border rhetoric unless tied to concrete governance moves.
Exclude unrelated foreign-policy migration stories without domestic coercive implications.
boundary_notes: Related to civil-rights rollback, but focused on status, deportability, and belonging.
Related to law-as-weapon, but centered on immigration machinery rather than prosecution generally.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Law Enforcement and Justice Reoriented Toward Impunity for Allies and Punishment of Opponents
candidate_threads.description: Repurposing DOJ, pardons, prosecutions, watchdog removals, and enforcement priorities to protect regime allies, erase accountability, and pressure perceived enemies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil rights enforcement is frozen while law is bent to protect regime-aligned causes
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces pardons, selective clemency, and withdrawal of protections as a legal inversion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump weaponizes law and pardons to erase January 6 accountability and shield himself
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes explicit the combination of pardons, purges, and record erasure to protect insiders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Justice Department, FBI, and oversight mechanisms are purged and repurposed to shield Trump and allies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Expands the pattern into DOJ, FBI, election, labor, and oversight institutions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and justice are repurposed to shield allies and target enemies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the pattern broadening into anti-corruption rollback, case intervention, and judicial intimidation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Justice System Bent Toward Regime Protection and Impunity for Allies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms continuity through prosecutorial manipulation, pardons, and selective enforcement.

aliases: law bent to protect regime-aligned causes
inclusion_notes: Include pardons, dropped or redirected cases, watchdog removals, prosecutorial intervention, and reorientation of enforcement priorities.
Include attacks on judges and oversight where directly tied to legal impunity or coercion.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general executive overreach unless it specifically affects justice or enforcement.
Exclude immigration enforcement unless the legal manipulation itself is the point.
boundary_notes: Related to administrative state capture, but focused on law, prosecution, and accountability.
Related to information control when records are erased, but the core thread is justice-system transformation.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Civil Rights, Gender, and Reproductive Freedom Rolled Back to Enforce a Narrower Social Order
candidate_threads.description: Coordinated rollback of DEI, transgender rights, reproductive autonomy, and broader equality protections to embed a more exclusionary and nationalist social hierarchy.

supporting_developments.development_title: DEI, gender, and reproductive rights are rolled back to enforce a narrower social order
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the week-one anti-DEI, anti-trans, and anti-reproductive-rights framework.

supporting_developments.development_title: DEI, LGBTQ+ rights, and civic education are dismantled across government, schools, and prisons
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the thread spreading into schools, prisons, the military, and public commemorations.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil and human rights are rolled back along lines of gender, race, religion, and punishment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Broadens the social-order logic to punishment, religion, and race as well as gender.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and public health are redefined along ideological and identity lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the same exclusionary hierarchy being applied to public-health and identity protections.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civic Education, Culture, and Public Memory Are Rewritten Along Ideological Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the rights rollback into education, memory, and institutional culture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Coordinated assault on transgender people and DEI across government, schools, and culture
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms sustained focus on trans people and DEI across multiple state systems.

inclusion_notes: Include attacks on DEI, transgender rights, reproductive rights, race-conscious equality measures, and identity-based access to public institutions.
Include ideological or religious framing when used to justify these exclusions.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic education policy unless it clearly advances the exclusionary social-order project.
Exclude immigration-specific status rules unless the core issue is identity-based rights rollback rather than deportability.
boundary_notes: Related to information and cultural control, but centered on rights, identity, and legal-social hierarchy.
May overlap with citizenship stratification when identity-based exclusions are embedded in status rules.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information Control, Archive Manipulation, and Memory Rewriting
candidate_threads.description: Restriction, deletion, reframing, and politicization of data, media access, archives, public language, and cultural memory in order to shape what the public can know and remember.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control and propaganda reshape what the public can see and believe
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces data suppression, propaganda framing, and symbolic rewriting as a governing method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, archives, and symbolism are curated to erase inconvenient realities and glorify the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Expands the pattern into archives, holidays, naming, and public symbolism.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, media access, and public memory are systematically manipulated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the same logic applied to media access, state data, and platform power.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, memory, and culture are aggressively rewritten to fit regime narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes archive control, cultural rewriting, and Stonewall/history edits central.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information Control Tightens: Media Punished, Data Seized, and Critics Cast as Threats
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds media punishment and data seizure to the already-running memory-control thread.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and culture brought under tighter political control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms the thread through media access restrictions, language control, and cultural pressure.

inclusion_notes: Include deletion or alteration of public data, archive control, media access retaliation, symbolic renaming, narrative engineering, and culture-war memory interventions.
Include use of private platforms where they clearly reinforce state-favored information control.
exclusion_notes: Exclude ordinary political messaging unless tied to suppression, deletion, or coercive narrative control.
Exclude generic disinformation unless embedded in institutional manipulation of information channels.
boundary_notes: Related to law-as-weapon where records are deleted to protect allies, but broader than legal accountability alone.
Related to rights rollback when culture and curriculum are rewritten, but focused on information and memory systems.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Crony Capitalism and Fusion of State Power with Private Insider Networks
candidate_threads.description: Blurring of public power and private enrichment through crypto, family ventures, donor-friendly regulation, privileged access, sovereign-investment concepts, and billionaire influence over public decisions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and personal enrichment are woven into core economic policy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the fusion of public policy with family and insider gain.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and billionaire influence blur the line between public office and private gain
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows insider networks and billionaires moving from adjacent influence into governance.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and Trump family ventures intertwine with state power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms the Trump-family and ally-business dimension as a recurring thread, not a one-off.

supporting_developments.development_title: Austerity and Fossil-Fuel Policy Shift Economic Burdens Onto the Vulnerable
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows how broader economic policy choices align with insider and fossil-fuel interests.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and regulation bent to favor donors and regime-aligned business
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows direct regulatory favoritism for donors and politically aligned business actors.

aliases: Trump family ventures and state power
inclusion_notes: Include donor-aligned enforcement decisions, family ventures tied to policy, privileged insider access, crypto and sovereign-fund schemes, and billionaire operational influence.
Include economic or regulatory moves when their beneficiary logic is clearly insider-facing.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general economic policy unless the insider-beneficiary or fusion element is clear.
Exclude pure administrative capture unless private enrichment or private governance is central.
boundary_notes: Related to administrative state capture when private actors acquire operating leverage, but focused on enrichment and patronage rather than bureaucracy alone.
Related to foreign-policy personalization where business interests influence diplomacy.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Executive Overreach Through Emergency Rule, Spending Freezes, and White House Control of Independent Power Centers
candidate_threads.description: Use of emergencies, funding freezes, impoundment logic, and direct presidential control over supposedly independent or congressionally constrained functions to expand unilateral power.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump’s second inauguration unleashes a blitz of unilateral power grabs
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes emergency-driven unilateralism and early statute-defying behavior.

supporting_developments.development_title: Emergency powers and funding freezes test the limits of executive control over the purse
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Places control over the purse and emergency governance at the center of the thread.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive impoundment and fiscal brinkmanship weaponize the power of the purse
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms that impoundment and fiscal coercion are continuing methods rather than transitional tactics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Power Sidesteps Congress and Courts to Centralize Control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the thread extending into independent agencies, spending, and direct confrontation with judicial limits.

aliases: White House control over independent agencies
inclusion_notes: Include emergency declarations, funding freezes, impoundment-like behavior, reprogramming efforts, and White House control of independent agencies or regulatory bodies.
Include fiscal brinkmanship when used as an instrument of presidential power.
exclusion_notes: Exclude routine budgeting or policy disputes without clear constitutional overreach.
Exclude DOGE staffing moves unless the emphasis is on separation-of-powers erosion rather than bureaucratic capture.
boundary_notes: Related to administrative state capture, but more constitutional and fiscal in emphasis.
Related to foreign-policy unilateralism where emergency or executive power substitutes for congressional process.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Foreign Policy, Multilateral Retreat, and National Security Personalized Around the Presidency
candidate_threads.description: Rapid retreat from multilateral commitments, personalization of diplomacy and security decision-making, and use of foreign policy as a transactional extension of executive ideology and private influence.

supporting_developments.development_title: Foreign policy and multilateral commitments are abruptly reversed and partially privatized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces multilateral retreat and privatized substitutes as a foundational external-policy shift.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and security agencies are reoriented toward spectacle and regime protection
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the security-state side of the same personalized and theatrical foreign-policy posture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power and foreign policy are radically centralized through aid freezes, tariffs, and multilateral withdrawals
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes centralized foreign-policy control and multilateral withdrawal explicit.

supporting_developments.development_title: Foreign policy and national security are personalized, transactional, and destabilizing
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms the thread through transactional diplomacy, appointments, and security personalization.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power defies oversight at home and reorients foreign policy abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Links foreign-policy realignment directly to executive overreach and exclusion of institutional constraints.

inclusion_notes: Include withdrawals from international institutions, unilateral arms and aid decisions, personalized diplomacy, and politicized national-security appointments or operations.
Include private or family-linked influence over foreign-policy direction where clear.
exclusion_notes: Exclude ordinary foreign-policy disagreements absent a pattern of unilateral personalization.
Exclude immigration-only stories unless they directly reshape foreign or security posture.
boundary_notes: Related to executive overreach, but specific to foreign, security, and multilateral domains.
Related to crony capitalism where business interests bleed into diplomacy.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Education, Culture, and Public Institutions Reshaped to Enforce Regime Ideology
candidate_threads.description: Pressure on schools, universities, arts institutions, libraries, curricula, and cultural bodies to erase disfavored histories and identities while advancing regime-aligned narratives.

supporting_developments.development_title: DEI, LGBTQ+ rights, and civic education are dismantled across government, schools, and prisons
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces education and institutional culture as sites of ideological restructuring.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, memory, and culture are aggressively rewritten to fit regime narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern into cultural institutions, archives, and historical memory.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civic Education, Culture, and Public Memory Are Rewritten Along Ideological Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers education and culture capture explicitly as a recurring development.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and culture brought under tighter political control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows continued control over language, arts, and educational discourse.

supporting_developments.development_title: University and campus control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: The week-seven structural themes explicitly identify universities and campuses as a distinct area of control and pressure.

inclusion_notes: Include school curricula, university pressure, library and book interventions, arts and commemorative institutions, and public-memory restructuring when used to impose ideology.
Include institutional defunding or censorship tied to these cultural-educational goals.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic media control unless schools, universities, arts, or institutional memory are central.
Exclude rights rollbacks that do not materially reshape institutions of learning or culture.
boundary_notes: Related to information and memory control, but focused on institutionalized culture and education rather than data or media systems alone.
Related to rights rollback where targeted identities are erased through cultural institutions.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Courts, States, Unions, and Civil Society Mount Reactive but Persistent Resistance
candidate_threads.description: A recurring counter-thread in which courts, states, unions, media, and civic actors challenge executive actions, slow implementation, and preserve fragments of institutional constraint.

supporting_developments.development_title: States, courts, and civil society mount early resistance to Trump’s agenda
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces resistance as a recurring but reactive counter-current.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts, states, and civil society mount reactive but limited resistance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms the same pattern across litigation, organizing, and state-level counteraction.

supporting_developments.development_title: States, courts, and civil society mount fragmented but significant resistance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows that resistance remains meaningful but structurally fragmented.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts, civil society, and local actors mount fragmented but real resistance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the thread through injunctions, protests, and local institutional response.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public and Bureaucratic Resistance Emerges but Remains Fragmented
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows resistance moving inside the bureaucracy as well as outside it.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public backlash and allied responses highlight emerging lines of resistance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms that backlash continues, but still in uneven and domain-specific forms.

aliases: courts and civil society push back
inclusion_notes: Include injunctions, lawsuits, state countermeasures, union action, protests, and bureaucratic resignations or refusals when they function as checks on executive consolidation.
Include international or allied responses when they materially signal resistance to the same domestic-authoritarian moves.
exclusion_notes: Exclude isolated positive governance acts unless they meaningfully counter a recurring authoritarian thread.
Exclude routine judicial or legislative actions without clear oppositional significance.
boundary_notes: This is a counter-thread rather than a regime method, but it recurs strongly enough within the window to merit separate tracking.
Should remain distinct from week-specific scandal or protest coverage.

notes_on_window: The clearest sustained threads in this window are administrative state capture, immigration as coercive status hierarchy, rights rollback, information control, and reactive resistance.
Several weekly development titles vary in phrasing but cluster strongly around the same underlying patterns rather than truly distinct topics.
The evidence shown most clearly supports Weeks 1-7 for multiple threads; later weeks in the window likely continue some of these arcs but were not necessary to establish candidate continuity.
